Decrypt a JWE

Source: R/jwe.R
jose_decrypt.Rd

jose_decrypt() decrypts a JWE in any serialization. The caller names the key management algorithms and the content encryption algorithms it accepts; neither has a default. A token with zip is refused (RFC 8725 section 3.6).

Usage

jose_decrypt(token, key, algorithms, encryptions, limits = jose_limits())

Arguments

token

The JWE: a compact serialization, or JSON text.

key

A jose_key, a jose_keyset, or a function of the header returning one.

algorithms

The key management algorithms to accept, such as "A256KW".

encryptions

The content encryption algorithms to accept, such as "A256CBC-HS512".

limits

Resource limits, from jose_limits().

Value

A list of class jose_decrypted with plaintext (raw), header (the protected, shared and per-recipient headers merged), protected, and the kid, alg and enc that decrypted it.

Details

RSA1_5 is decrypted only when algorithms names it. It is exposed to Bleichenbacher-style attacks (RFC 8725 section 3.2); a padding failure is replaced by a random content key, as RFC 7516 section 11.5 asks, so that it fails exactly as a wrong key does. Prefer RSA-OAEP-256.

Every failure after the header checks (a wrong key, a bad tag, bad padding, a failed key unwrap, a wrong length) raises the same zujose_decrypt_error with the same message, so that the error cannot tell an attacker which step failed (RFC 7516 section 11.5).

With several recipients, those whose algorithm is not in algorithms, or for whom key holds no key, are skipped; decryption succeeds with the first recipient it can decrypt for.

Examples

# RFC 7516 Appendix A.3.
token <- paste0(
  "eyJhbGciOiJBMTI4S1ciLCJlbmMiOiJBMTI4Q0JDLUhTMjU2In0.",
  "6KB707dM9YTIgHtLvtgWQ8mKwboJW3of9locizkDTHzBC2IlrT1oOQ.",
  "AxY8DCtDaGlsbGljb3RoZQ.",
  "KDlTtXchhZTGufMYmOYGS4HffxPSUrfmqCHXaI9wOGY.",
  "U0m_YmjN04DJvceFICbCVQ"
)
key <- as_jose_key('{"kty":"oct","k":"GawgguFyGrWKav7AX4VKUg"}')
out <- jose_decrypt(token, key, "A128KW", "A128CBC-HS256")
rawToChar(out$plaintext)
#> [1] "Live long and prosper."
